mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each natural person beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in country of origin or Luxembourg notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for non-EU Hague Convention countries; consular legalization for non-Hague countries

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of registered address of the SCSp (lease agreement or registered office agreement)
Certificate of good standing or excerpt from foreign commercial register (for corporate general partners)
Draft partnership agreement / articles of association of the SCSp (Acte de Société)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary (or private writing if admitted under LSC)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or source-of-funds evidence for the initial contribution

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all proposed UBOs, general partners, and authorized signatories against: (i) EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (ii) UN Security Council Consolidated List; (iii) OFAC SDN List (as a prudent risk-control measure for USD-linked activity); (iv) national Luxembourg PEP database and justice ministry blacklists; and (v) CSSF AML/CFT guidelines. Screening must be documented, archived for five years, and refreshed annually or upon any beneficial-ownership change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / RCS electronic filing via MyGuichet.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be submitted in French, German, or Luxembourgish, or in any language using Latin script. Non-Latin script names must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet. The name must be distinctive, not misleading, and not contrary to public order or good morals. Luxembourg law does not require a particular language for partnership names, but the RCS will reject names that are confusingly similar to existing registered names or protected public names.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Luxembourg (if used alone or in a misleading way without prior authorization)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon RCS rejection, the applicant may request a reasoned written refusal from the RCS within 15 days of the online decision. An administrative appeal must then be lodged with the Directeur de l'Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA within two months of notification. Alternatively, a direct action on the merits may be filed before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (Chambre commerciale). The applicant may also submit a revised name via MyGuichet.lu. Extension of an accepted name reservation is not permitted beyond the initial 60-day window; the applicant must submit a new reservation application, which is not automatically granted if the name has become unavailable.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual or service-provider registered office is permissible in Luxembourg for an SCSp provided that the office constitutes a physical Luxembourg address where the RCS and tax authorities can deliver documents and where corporate records may be inspected. Pure mailbox-only arrangements without any personnel or physical access are not acceptable. A professional corporate service provider (PSF, e.g., a fiduciaire or registered agent) is normally engaged for this purpose, and the registered office must appear in the partnership agreement and be filed with the RCS.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 10% annual probability for a low-risk, asset-light reverse logistics SCSp managed by a regulated PSF; increases to 25-30% if the SCSp is self-managed or acts as a conduit for intra-group flows. The RCS and the Administration de l'enregistrement may perform unannounced visits, and under the RBE law, the Luxembourg Business Registers may request supporting documents as part of UBO verification.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration fee of EUR 75-100 plus publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market flat annual fee for registered office, mail handling, and RBE/RCS compliance support.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing bank issuance fee (or nil if internal verification); includes document apostille/notarization cost.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Amended Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), SCSp chapter as introduced by the Law of 12 July 2013 and restated by the Law of 23 June 2016; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 September 2016 on the RCS; Law of 19 December 2008 on the electronic register and e-filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); registration duty collected by the Recette d'enregistrement of the Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AED).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: RCS electronic incorporation declaration (Formulaire C — SCSp) filed on the lbr.lu e-filing portal, accompanied by the executed partnership agreement (contrat de société), identity documents of the associé gérant and partners, and proof of registered office.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for an SCSp; zero or flexible capital permitted. No escrow account, capital deposit certificate, or bank attestation is required by company law. Contributions are allocated to individual capital accounts in the partnership agreement, and paid-up amounts are subject only to AML/KYC verification at bank account opening.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: UNANIMOUS WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE PARTNERS OF SCSp [•], dated [••] 2025, adopted in lieu of a meeting: 1. The partnership agreement (contrat de société) is approved in its final form. 2. The initial capital subscriptions of the limited partners are accepted; no statutory minimum capital being mandatory, contributions are credited to individual capital accounts. 3. The registered office (siège social) is fixed at [address], Luxembourg. 4. [Name] is appointed associé gérant (general manager) with sole power to represent the SCSp, including opening bank accounts with Airwallex and local ACH providers. 5. The associé gérant is instructed to file the registration with the RCS and to complete post-filing formalities. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Availability Check and Pre-Filing Eligibility Review
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — RCS online registry search and e-filing pre-check (lbr.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the RCS database to confirm that the proposed SCSp denomination is distinguishable from existing registered names. Verify that the ISIC 5229 reverse-logistics scope is an unregulated commercial activity under the liberalized establishment regime and that no sectoral license is triggered. Confirm the identity and eligibility of the general partner (associé gérant) and initial limited partner, and collect the registered-office address for the pre-filing checklist.
required_dossiers: Proposed SCSp name with 2 alternative names
Identity documents of the general partner and limited partner
Registered office address or letter of intent from the lessor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected as confusingly similar, file a revised name request via the LBR portal; a new availability confirmation is issued within one business day and does not restart the filing fee obligation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Partnership Agreement and Appointment of the Gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Partners acting by private deed (notarization optional); consular legalization/apostille authority for foreign signatures; if notarized, a Luxembourg notary registered with the Association des Notaires du Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Finalize the contrat de société in French or in English with a French annex, incorporating the first written resolution, capital-account schedule, and registered-office clause. Obtain signatures of all partners and the consent of the appointed associé gérant. If executed abroad, legalize or apostille foreign signatures in accordance with the Hague 1961 Convention and, where required, provide certified translations by a Luxembourg sworn translator.
required_dossiers: Written acceptance of the associé gérant
Certified copies of passports and proof of residence of partners
Registered-office lease or letter of intent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AED or RCS challenges signature authenticity or incomplete annexes, obtain an apostille/legalization for foreign signatures, attach sworn translations, and resubmit the entire instrument for re-registration within the 15-day response window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Registration Duty to the AED
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AED) — Recette d'enregistrement (counter at the RCS desk or eCDF online payment)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Lodge the executed instrument with the AED and pay the fixed registration duty assessed for the partnership agreement (EUR 25 for a private deed, EUR 75 for a notarial deed). Obtain a stamped or electronically endorsed copy (timbre de réception) evidencing payment; this proof must be attached to the RCS filing.
required_dossiers: AED duty payment request (formulaire de paiement)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the duty is under-assessed or the deed lacks annexes, pay the shortfall on the same day through the eCDF portal and obtain an updated receipt; the earlier date of submission is preserved if the cure is completed within one business day.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) — Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration, responsible for corporate income tax, municipal business tax, net wealth tax and the national business matricule; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) — Registration, Estates and VAT Administration, competent for VAT registration, VAT returns, export-evidence verification and VAT refunds. Digital access: MyGuichet.lu (single e-government gateway), the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) for RCS commercial-register filings, and the ACD/AEDT electronic filing portals (eCDF / MyGuichet secure workspace) for tax returns and correspondence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step-by-step for a Luxembourg SCSp and its foreign co-investors: (1) notarised constitution of the SCSp followed by registration with the RCS (Luxembourg Business Registers), which automatically generates the national business matricule (the identification number used by the ACD for direct-tax purposes and by the AEDT for VAT matching); (2) application to the AEDT for the Luxembourg VAT identification number before commencing taxable trade, submitted via MyGuichet.lu using the official VAT-registration form (formulaire 640) accompanied by the RCS excerpt, the partnership agreement and the identity of the general partner; (3) a non-resident enterprise without a Luxembourg establishment (e.g., foreign principal or logistics operator) carrying out taxable supplies or services in Luxembourg must obtain a Luxembourg VAT number or apply the domestic reverse-charge where available; if established outside the EU, it must appoint a Luxembourg joint-and-severally liable VAT representative and file an irrevocable power of attorney; (4) after documentary vetting — no minimum capital, no licence and no guarantee are required for this low-risk reverse-logistics scope — the AEDT issues the VAT number with the LU prefix; (5) the SCSp then files periodic VAT returns through eCDF and may apply for VAT refunds, including under the special EU refund mechanism for non-established taxable persons.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The SCSp is a fiscally transparent partnership by operation of law; no election is needed for pass-through direct-tax treatment. Luxembourg nevertheless provides several statutory mechanisms: (a) an implicit VAT election — the partnership can be treated as an independent taxable person for VAT where it conducts an entrepreneurial activity, allowing the SCSp to centralise VAT registration, invoicing and input-VAT recovery; (b) the small-business franchise option to remain outside VAT below the EUR 30,000 turnover threshold, or to waive the exemption by optional registration; (c) the VAT-grouping election (assujetti unique) combining the SCSp with affiliated taxable persons into a single taxable person; (d) the EU-wide One-Stop-Shop and Import One-Stop-Shop elections for distance sales and import transactions; and (e) the hybrid-mismatch alignment and neutralisation rules transposing ATAD and the anti-hybrid Directive, under which a partner's interest in a transparent SCSp may be re-profiled where a foreign jurisdiction treats the SCSp as opaque; such arrangements must be disclosed in the Luxembourg corporate tax return. Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box system and there is no separate municipal registration beyond the single national tax identifier.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA — Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: General mandatory VAT registration threshold under the small-business franchise: annual net taxable turnover of EUR 30,000 (in force from 1 January 2025; previously EUR 25,000). Businesses below the threshold may voluntarily register and thereby deduct input VAT; exceeding the threshold terminates the franchise. For cross-border distance sales of goods, the EU-wide EUR 10,000 OSS threshold applies. A non-established foreign vendor has no domestic turnover threshold and must register for all Luxembourg taxable supplies, except where the place-of-supply rule allocates the supply to another EU Member State, the customer is liable under the reverse charge, or the sale is declared under the OSS/IOSS special schemes.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg imposes no real-time fiscal pre-clearance, no tax-authority invoice stamping and no mandatory B2B/B2C continuous transaction controls. The operative mandates are: (i) B2G e-invoicing through the national PEPPOL access point under the EN 16931 standard for public-procurement contracts; (ii) VAT-law requirements on invoice content, sequential numbering, issue dates and preservation of originals; (iii) the GOBD formal data-management obligations (ACD guidance of 2021) covering archiving, immutability, chronological traceability and accessibility of electronic books and source documents for audit; and (iv) electronic filing of all VAT returns, EC sales lists and Intrastat declarations through the AEDT portal on the statutory monthly or quarterly cycle. The AEDT therefore performs periodic, risk-based clearance through fraud-detection analytics rather than immediate clearance of each invoice.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for: (1) export supplies of goods — including returned merchandise, quality-graded goods, repaired or refurbished outputs, and recyclable scrap — where the goods are dispatched or transported by or on behalf of the supplier to a destination outside the EU customs territory; the supplier must be identified as exporter or hold the export mandate, and proof of departure from the EU must exist no later than the filing of the relevant VAT return; (2) ancillary services connected with exported goods (handling, packing, inspection, quality grading, testing, repair, freight and insurance) rendered in Luxembourg to the non-EU owner or non-EU customer, provided the supporting evidence links each service to the specific exported goods; (3) intra-Community supplies of goods to VAT-registered customers in another EU Member State, which are exempt with credit (equivalent to zero-rating) against the customer's valid EU VAT number and compliant dispatch documentation; and (4) B2B services supplied to non-EU recipients that fall outside Luxembourg VAT under the general customer-location place-of-supply rule. The zero-rate is strictly construed; identical services supplied to a Luxembourg customer are taxable at 17%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic SAD/AES declaration in the ECS-2 environment, with validated exit confirmation from the EU customs office of exit), naming the SCSp as exporter or the principal party;
Bill of Lading (sea), Air Waybill (air), CMR or rail consignment note (combined transport document) evidencing physical dispatch from Luxembourg and arrival outside the EU customs territory;

Commercial invoice together with the reverse-logistics file: return-merchandise authorisation, warehouse receipt, quality-grading certificate, repair/refurbishment work order or scrap/disposal certificate proving commercial substance;

Payment and inward remittance evidence: bank transfer records, SWIFT reference, or Airwallex/Local ACH transaction reports demonstrating receipt of the export consideration and its repatriation where applicable;
EC sales list / Intrastat filing proof and the customer's EU VAT identification number where the supply is intra-Community;
Any sampling, valuation or customs-supervision documentation required by the customs office during post-clearance audit.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg applies a strict evidentiary standard to export zero-rating; every claim must be substantiated at the time the VAT return is filed and retained for ten years under GOBD rules. Penal consequences include: (i) recharacterisation of the supply as domestic taxable at 17% with clawback of VAT plus statutory late-payment interest (intérêts de retard) from the original filing date; (ii) administrative fines of up to EUR 25,000 per offence for false or missing export evidence, invoicing irregularities, or refusal to produce the export file; (iii) criminal prosecution for deliberate tax fraud (fraude fiscale under Luxembourg criminal tax law and the Criminal Code), exposing the general partner and, given the transparency of the SCSp, the limited partners to fines of up to EUR 250,000 and custodial penalties of one to five years; (iv) application of the anti-abuse doctrine and Luxembourg arm's-length rules where the transaction lacks commercial substance (e.g., circular trade, fictitious returns, switched bills of lading), with reversal of the burden of proof and increased sanctions; and (v) freezing or set-off of VAT refunds, suspension of the VAT identification number, and publication of sanctions. Repatriation and export evidence must be completed within 180 days of the underlying export, failing which a discretionary clawback procedure may be opened.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) and the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) jointly regulate banking and treasury activity; Luxembourg operates within the European System of Central Banks, with the European Central Bank setting monetary policy and the euro as lawful tender.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg applies full current and capital account convertibility under the EU Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (Articles 63–66 TFEU) and the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements. No restrictions apply to foreign direct investment, profit remittance, repatriation of capital, or liquidation proceeds for EU/EEA and most third-country investors, provided the underlying transaction is documented, the UBO chain is transparent, and no sanctions or anti-money-laundering concerns exist. Payments may be made in EUR or any reserve currency; conversion is freely undertaken by credit institutions at prevailing market rates. Remittance of distributions from an SCSp to non-resident partners is treated as a pass-through profit share and is not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax, but a beneficiary self-declaration and Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) extract should be provided.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds exists in Luxembourg. Export receipts from the reverse-logistics return of goods may be credited directly to a EUR or foreign-currency account. If a bank receipt is in a third-country currency, the foreign currency may be kept or converted at the entity's option. For statistical reporting, payments exceeding thresholds are declared to the BCL via the reporting agent (the bank) using the EUR/ECA payment code for services or trade; no conversion ratio applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Foreign Currency Sweep
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility for near-term payment processing through EU/EEA licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) such as Airwallex, but limited to payment initiation and e-money safeguarding. EMIs cannot grant credit, provide derivative hedging, or maintain fiduciary deposit accounts. Legal constraints require the EMI to hold funds in a segregated safeguarding account at a Luxembourg or EU-licensed credit institution; the SCSp should therefore keep its main capital base in a tier-1 credit institution and use the EMI only as a disbursement/collection rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical on-site interview is generally required for the first commercial relationship between a Luxembourg bank and a newly established SCSp, particularly because the partnership is not a legal entity subject to full corporate transparency in all jurisdictions. Authorized signatories (general partner representative or manager) must appear in person with valid passports and, where requested, the local notary who executed the partnership deed. Remote onboarding via eIDAS-qualified digital identification and video verification is legally possible, but Luxembourg banks retain discretion and often require a physical meet-and-greet for SCSp structures with non-resident ultimate beneficial owners before activating treasury lines.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pass-through SCSp with no minimum capital and no statutory obligation to file annual accounts; banks may classify it as high-risk if partners are undisclosed.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide notarised and apostilled partnership agreement (contrat de société), CSSF/BCL register extract, Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) extract showing all partners, notarised declarations of ultimate control, and a written business-plan memorandum detailing the reverse-logistics economic substance, warehouse contracts, staff structure, and projected annual flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBOs or investors domiciled in high-risk third countries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Passport copies, proof of residential address, source-of-funds documentation (bank statements, audited financials, transactional trail), sanctions and adverse-media screening screenshots, and a compliance sign-off by the AML reporting officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Industry characteristic: returned goods valuation, repair and remarketing may look like cash-intensive or high-refund-volume money-laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply contractual framework with marketplace/e-commerce client, standardised returns workflow, valuation/grading reports, sample invoices, refund ledger, and an anti-money-laundering risk assessment mapping the business flow to legitimate commercial activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected frequent cross-border outbound disbursements to third-country suppliers without clear documentation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approved vendor list, purchase orders, logistics bills of lading, inspection certificates, customs declarations, and a copy of the MT103 payment sanction-screening procedure.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound route: (a) SEPA Instant / SEPA Credit Transfer in EUR for shareholders' capital contributions up to €100,000 per transaction; (b) SWIFT MT103 for larger or non-EUR contributions, with the beneficiary's BIC (Luxembourg BICXXX), IBAN, and exact legal name 'LU SCSp'. Payment instruction must reference the capital contribution notice, the SCSp's RBE number, and, for statistical purposes, a purpose code that the receiving bank maps to 'foreign direct investment capital contribution' (e.g., Luxembourg BCL balance-of-payments code for equity capital; if unsure, require the bank's regulatory reporting team to attach the correct EBA/BCL purpose code). For EUR wires from outside the eurozone, TARGET2 settlement is used, and the sender's bank must include the ISO 20022 structured remittance tag or SWIFT field 70 containing 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION / SCSP / [entity reference]'. Verification at the bank includes match on name/IBAN, positive sanctions screening, and, if the amount exceeds €10,000, a source-of-funds declaration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For settlement of returned-goods supplier invoices and logistics fees: use SEPA Credit Transfer for EU/EEA beneficiaries; SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA beneficiaries (field 70 detail: 'INV [invoice number] / REVERSE LOGISTICS'); commercial letters of credit (UCP600) are recommended when disbursement is tied to shipping documents; for East Asia/US transactions, an MT103 with documentary LC or bank payment obligation is used. The SCSp's Luxembourg bank will apply the exchange rate, deduct charges (OUR/SHA/BEN), and perform OFAC/EU sanctions checks. For Airwallex or other EMI rails, outbound payments can be initiated in USD via SWIFT or local clearing, but the underlying funds must have been converted in a segregated account and the payee must match the invoice to avoid rejections.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright EUR/USD and EUR/GBP forward foreign exchange contracts (maturity ≤ 12 months)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for settlement in EUR against currencies of jurisdictions with exchange control restrictions (e.g., CNY, INR) executed under an ISDA 1998 Master Agreement
FX swaps (spot-forward combinations) for short-term liquidity re-profiling
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP) for rolling hedging of receivables and payables
Money-market deposits and euro-denominated index instruments for temporary cash parking

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (RBE declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RBE – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month following the anniversary date of initial RBE registration; annually thereafter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 1,250; criminal penalties up to EUR 125,000 and/or imprisonment for non-compliance; administrative strike-off risk for persistent neglect.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts and consolidated accounts (filing with RCS) – applicable if SCSp qualifies as a large undertaking, financial holding, or public entity; otherwise exempt
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of the financial year end (e.g., for a 31 December year-end, by 31 July of the following year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Compulsory filing enforcement by RCS; civil and criminal liability for managers; fines per Article 167 of the Law of 10 August 1915; possible court-ordered filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax and municipal business tax return (if at least one general partner is a corporate entity; otherwise tax-transparent, partner-level return applies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Luxembourg tax authorities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 May of the following year for calendar-year taxpayers, with possible extension to 31 December upon request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest of 0.6% per month on unpaid tax; late-filing penalties up to 10% of due tax; administrative fines; criminal sanctions for severe cases.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Audit required if the SCSp exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds at the balance sheet date: total balance sheet EUR 4,400,000; net turnover EUR 8,800,000; average of 50 employees during the financial year. Audit also mandatory for financial holdings, securitisation vehicles, or public issuers.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 19 December 2002 on the annual accounts of undertakings); IFRS as adopted by the EU permitted for certain undertakings or if the SCSp is publicly traded.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must maintain an RBE file and confirm the accuracy of beneficial ownership data annually within one month of the registration anniversary. Share transfer transactions during the year must be reflected in the RBE file and reconfirmed upon any change, in addition to the annual confirmation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (including partner resolutions and management decisions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Common range: USD 1,600 – 5,500 per year depending on service provider and complexity
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Typical audit fee range for a mid-sized reverse logistics SCSp: USD 5,400 – 21,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate Luxembourg City rate for FY2024 (CIT 17% + unemployment fund surcharge 7% of CIT = 1.19% + municipal business tax 6.75%); the SCSp is tax-transparent for income tax, so CIT applies at the partner level, while Municipal Business Tax applies at entity level because reverse logistics is a commercial activity under Art. 14 LIR.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP Box: 80% exemption of qualifying IP net income (effective ~4.99%); participation exemption: 100% exemption of qualifying dividends (>=10% holding or >=EUR 1.2m acquisition cost, 12-month holding) and capital gains; investment tax credit up to 13% on qualifying new investments; no net wealth tax on the SCSp; no dividend withholding tax on SCSp profit allocations to partners.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 670 / partnership information return (Déclaration spéciale de société de personnes) filed electronically via MyGuichet.lu (Espace entreprises, eCDF/eTax module); the SCSp does not file Form 690 (capital-company CIT return) unless it irrevocably elects full corporate taxation.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Fiscal year ending 31 December: due by 31 December of the following year (e.g., FY2024 return due 31 Dec 2025); non-calendar fiscal year: due within 5 months of fiscal-year close; mandatory electronic filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership identification: SCSp name, RCS number, tax matricule (N° d'identification), legal form, registered office address, fiscal year start/end dates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the Luxembourg tax representative's details if all partners are non-residents or the SCSp has no full Luxembourg administrative establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Activity description and NACE code (52.29 - other supporting transport activities; reverse logistics and returned-goods grading); confirm premises, staff, and operational assets in Luxembourg.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate the address of any Luxembourg permanent establishment and the extent of foreign-partner involvement in its management.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: For each general and limited partner: full name, address, country of tax residence, foreign tax ID, profit-share percentage, capital contribution, allocated share of SCSp taxable income/loss.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must attach home-country TRC and the DTA article invoked; Luxembourg tax is assessed on the Luxembourg-source commercial income allocated to them.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total net commercial income/loss, statutory add-backs and deductions, per-partner allocation reconciling to partnership accounting records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach financial statements; a non-resident partner may claim no Luxembourg tax on its share if the SCSp has no Luxembourg permanent establishment and the income is not Luxembourg-source.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers: formal reminder, then forced assessment (imposition d'office); late-payment interest of 0.6% per month; 10% late-payment surcharge; administrative fines up to EUR 25,000; criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years for willful non-filing or false declarations.
